title: Palauttivat auton korjattuna
subtitle: They returned the car as fixed

blocks.text: You know korjaantunut, the participle for 'got fixed', from Lesson 3. This lesson attaches a new ending to participles and nouns alike, to mark a state someone claims something is in — often the exact claim a reviewer is about to contradict. You'll also get -ksi, for things that become or are given for free.

blocks.translation: They returned the car as fixed.

blocks.title: A loaded little ending
blocks.text: In the actual review this line comes from, the car broke down again on the way home. Korjattuna — 'as [supposedly] fixed' — carries a quiet edge of doubt that the plain word korjattu wouldn't. Watch for this ending whenever a reviewer is reporting someone else's claim rather than a confirmed fact.
Piece 1 — Essive -na/-nä: being in a state or role

blocks.content: The {essive|grammar|case name|as/in the state of} case, ending in -na or -nä, marks a temporary state or role — 'as X', 'in the capacity of X'. Korjattu (fixed) → {korjattuna|grammar|essive|as fixed}. Takuu (warranty) → {takuuna|grammar|essive|as a warranty/under warranty} — used when a replacement part is given free because it's covered.

items.en: They returned the car as fixed.
It worked as a good example.

blocks.content: The {translative|grammar|case name|into/becoming/for} case, ending in -ksi, marks a change into a state, or 'for' in the sense of purpose. Ilmainen (free) → {ilmaiseksi|grammar|translative|for free} — literally 'becoming free', the standard way to say something was done at no cost. You'll see luvattiin korjata ilmaiseksi, 'promised to fix for free'.

items.en: They promised to fix their own mistake for free.

blocks.text: Piece 3 — Essive vs. translative: staying vs. becoming

blocks.title: One is a photo, the other is a video
blocks.text: Essive (-na/-nä) describes a state as it already is — a snapshot: korjattuna, 'as [already] fixed'. Translative (-ksi) describes movement into a new state — a transition: ilmaiseksi, 'becoming free / turning out to be free'. If nothing is changing, reach for essive. If something is turning into something else, reach for translative.

items.en: It was under warranty, for free.
My car was returned as fixed, but it wasn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: In what state did you get the car back?

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Sain sen korjattuna, mutta se hajosi jo kotimatkalla.
lines.en: I got it back as fixed, but it broke down already on the way home.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Did they then fix it for free?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: They promised to, but a bill came anyway.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Essive and translative both attach to words you already know: korjattu (Lesson 3's participle family) becomes korjattuna, ilmainen becomes ilmaiseksi. You're not learning new vocabulary here — you're learning two new endings to place on vocabulary you already own. That's the whole lesson.

blocks.content: Korjattuna: KOR-yat-tu-na (four even syllables, stress stays on KOR). Ilmaiseksi: IL-mai-sek-si (the 'ai' glides like 'eye', and the ending -ksi is crisp — don't soften the k). Takuuna: TA-kuu-na (long double 'uu' held clearly).

rows.en: as a warranty / under warranty (essive of takuu)
essive case — as/in the state of

blocks.title: What you now own
items: the essive -na/-nä: korjattuna, takuuna — describing an unchanging state
the translative -ksi: ilmaiseksi — describing a change into a state
you can tell the two apart: essive is a snapshot, translative is a transition
takuu and ilmainen, two very useful words for warranty and cost complaints
you can now read the subtle doubt reviewers plant with korjattuna when a claim later turns out false
